findings.label: Reverse halo sign on chest CT
findings.evidence: Caption explicitly describes bilateral ground-glass opacities with associated peripheral consolidations forming an atoll sign.

panels.rationale: Clear axial high-resolution chest CT from a patient with COP showing bilateral peripheral consolidations surrounding ground-glass opacity, producing the atoll/reverse-halo sign. The in-text identifies this pattern as less common in COP.
panels.attribution_text: Radzikowska and Fijolek. Update on cryptogenic organizing pneumonia.. Frontiers in medicine 2023. doi:10.3389/fmed.2023.1146782. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: High resolution computed tomography scan of a patient with COP. Bilateral ground glass opacities with associated peripheral consolidations forming an atoll sign.
in_text_mentions: d reticular fibrous changes may be present in peripheral parts of both lungs. Thickening around areas of ground glass opacity with an “atoll” or “crazy-paving” pattern may also be present, although it is less common. Additionally, nodular lesions, pleural thickening, and rarely enlargement of hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes, are present; emphysema or pleural effusion may also be observed (28–40). Honeycomb-type lesions are not in the spectrum of pulmonary changes observed in COP but might be evident in patients who exhibit interstitial pulmonary fibrosis with a component of OP (Figures 2–6).
